 Q.5) Describe Forward Error Correction versus Retransmission in detail. (4 Marks) 
During data transmission, errors may occur. To handle errors, two methods are used: 
1) Forward Error Correction (FEC) 
- In this method, the receiver corrects the error itself . 
- Sender adds extra bits called redundant bits  to the original data. 
- These bits help the receiver to detect and correct errors. 
- No need to resend the data . 
- Coding techniques (like Hamming code) are used. 
Working: 
Sender → adds redundant bits →

data . 
- Coding techniques (like Hamming code) are used. 
Working: 
Sender → adds redundant bits → sends coded data → receiver checks and corrects errors. 
Advantages 
- No retransmission required. 
- Fast communication. 
- Useful where retransmission is difficult (satellite communication). 
Disadvantages 
- Extra bits increase bandwidth. 
- More complex processing at receiver. 
2) Retransmission (ARQ – Automatic Repeat reQuest) 
- Receiver only detects error , not correct. 
- Receiver sends request to sender to send data again . 
- Message is resent until it is received correctly. 
Working: 
Sender sends data → receiver detects error → sends negative acknowledgement → sender 
retransmits. 
Advantages 
- Simple method. 
- Accurate data delivery. 
Disadvantages 
- Increases delay. 
- Reduces network performance.

 Q8) Describe ARQ (Automatic Repeat request) with example. (  4 Marks)  
ARQ (Automatic Repeat request) 
- ARQ is an error control method used in data communication. 
- In this technique, the receiver checks the received data . 
- If the data contains an error, the receiver asks the sender to send the data again 
(retransmission) . 
- Thus, ARQ ensures that the receiver gets the correct and original message . 
 Working of ARQ 
1. Sender transmits a data frame to the receiver. 
2. Receiver checks the frame using error detection method. 
3. If no error is found, receiver sends ACK (Acknowledgement)  to the sender. 
4. If error is found, receiver sends NACK (Negative Acknowledgement) . 
5. After receiving NACK, sender retransmits the same frame. 
6. This process continues until corr

. 
5. After receiving NACK, sender retransmits the same frame. 
6. This process continues until correct data is received. 
Example 
- Sender sends frame: 
- Sent Data:  1101010 
- Due to noise in channel receiver gets: 
- Received Data:  1100010 
- Here data is changed → error detected. 
- Receiver sends NACK to sender. 
- Sender retransmits frame again. 
- Receiver now receives correct data and sends ACK. 
Types of ARQ 
1. Stop-and-Wait ARQ 
2. Go-Back-N ARQ 
3. Selective Repeat ARQ 
 Advantages 
 Reliable data transmission. 
 Correct message is always received. 
 Simple to implement. 
Disadvantages 
 Retransmission causes delay. 
 Network performance decreases when errors are frequent.

- Repetition code  is a basic error detection and correction technique used in data 
communication. 
- In this method, each bit of the original data is repeated several times  before transmission. 
- The main purpose is to make communication more rel

s repeated several times  before transmission. 
- The main purpose is to make communication more reliable. 
- Instead of sending one bit once, the sender sends the same bit multiple times such as 3 times 
or 5 times. 
- At the receiver side, the received bits are checked and the original bit is decided using the 
majority voting rule . 
- If most of the received bits are 1, then the original bit is considered 1. 
- If most of the received bits are 0, then the original bit is considered 0. 
 Working 
1. Sender repeats every bit of data multiple times. 
2. Repeated bits are transmitted through the communication channel.

4. Receiver receives repeated bits. 
5. Receiver applies majority voting. 
6. Receiver recovers the original data.

CRC is a powerful error detection technique  used in data communication.

dancy Check (CRC) 
CRC is a powerful error detection technique  used in data communication. 
In this method, the sender and receiver agree on a fixed binary number called a generator 
polynomial (divisor) .Before transmission, extra bits called CRC bits (redundant bits)  are added to 
the data. At the receiver side, the same division is performed. If remainder is zero, data is correc t; 
otherwise error occurred. 
Working of CRC 
At Sender Side 
1. Take the original data bits (message). 
2. Append n-1 zeros to the data (where n = number of bits in generator). 
3. Divide the new data by generator polynomial using modulo-2 division  (binary division 
without carry/borrow). 
4. The remainder obtained is called CRC bits . 
5. Replace appended zeros with this remainder. 
6. Send the final data frame to receiver. 
  
At Receiver Side 
1. Receiver divides received data by the same generator polynomial. 
2. If remainder = 000…0 → No error. 
3. If remainder ≠ 0 → Error detected.

at the data link layer. 
Each frame contains sender address, receiver address, control information and data.

 Receiver automatically knows frame boundary.

 Q17) With the help of diagram describe 802.11 architecture. (6 Marks)  
IEEE 802.11 architecture  defines the structure of a Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) used in 
Wi-Fi communication.  
It explains how wireless devices communicate with each other using radio signals through an Access 
Point (AP).  
In this architecture, wireless devices such as laptops and mobiles are called stations (STA) . 
All stations communicate through a central device known as the Access Point . The access point 
connects the wireless network to the wired LAN or Internet.  
A group of stations connected to one access point forms a Basic Serv

to the wired LAN or Internet.  
A group of stations connected to one access point forms a Basic Service Set (BSS) . 
When multiple access points are connected together using a wired backbone network called 
Distribution System (DS) , it forms an Extended Service Set (ESS)  which increases the coverage 
area. 
 
Working:  
When a station sends data, it first goes to the access point.  
The access point checks the destination.  
If the receiver is in the same BSS, the AP sends data directly.  
If it belongs to another BSS, the data is forwarded through the distribution system to another access 
point. 
Advantages  
 Mobility support  
 Easy installation  
 No cabling required  
Disadvantages  
 Limited coverage area  
 Interference possible  
 Less secure than wired LAN

 Q20) Draw and explain Piconet Bluetooth architecture. (4 Marks)  
Piconet in Bluetooth  
A piconet is the basic network structure of Bluetooth communication.  
It is a small wireless network formed when Bluetooth devices connect with each other.  
In a piconet:  
 One device acts as Master 
 Maximum 7 active devices act as Slaves  
The master device controls communication and timing.  
All slave devices communicate only through the master device.  
 
 Working  
1. A Bluetooth device starts communication and becomes master.  
2. Other nearby Bluetooth devices join as slaves.  
3. Master assigns time slots to slaves.  
4. Data transfer takes place using radio signals (2.4 GHz band).  
 Advantages  
 Simple device connection  
 Low power consumption  
 No wires required  
Disadvantages  
 Limited number of devices  
 Short communication range

 Q21)  Draw and explain Scatternet Bluetooth architecture. (4 Marks)  
- A scatternet is a network formed by connecting two or more piconets.  
- A piconet is a small Bluetooth network with one master (primary) and multiple slaves 
(secondary devices).  
- In a scatternet, devices from different piconets are connected together.  
- A device from one piconet joins another piconet.  
- This device is called a bridge node . 
- The bridge connects multiple piconets and helps them communicate.  
- The bridge node works in two roles:  
- Acts as a slave in one piconet  
- Acts as a master in another piconet  
- It transfers data between different piconets.  
 
- The bridge node connects both piconets. 
- It transfers data  from one piconet to another.
